prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Reordering sign-in after pet or companion selection, generation countdown timers, pet control tutorial screens, personality headlines, path duration hints, and account safety or persistence hints consistently won.
Major redesigns, sub-flows, trait selectors, photo guidance copy, benefits story copy, estimated time headlines, account recovery hints, and reordering sign-in after photo upload hurt performance.
Notifications, layout modifications, incentives, permission checks, and wait screen activity tips showed no clear effect.
Flow bypasses yielded mixed results, winning in round 1 but hurting performance in round 3.
Predictions overestimated gains for major redesigns, sub-flows, copy changes, and reordering sign-in after photo upload.
Predictions underestimated gains for pet control tutorial screens, wait countdowns, personality headlines, path duration hints, and account safety or persistence hints.

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Pet Visibility and Hide Guide Screen: Adds a dedicated guide screen right after the home intro explaining how to toggle desktop pet visibility, move the pet, and access tray controls. (why: Support receives multiple emails about users being unclear on how to control, hide, or locate their pet on the desktop after setup.)
1: [sign_in, hint] Account Pet Retrieval Sign-In Hint: Adds a hint on the sign-in screen reassuring users that logging into an existing account restores previous pets. (why: 8 support emails complained about pets missing or reset after signing in again.)
2: [home, wait_info] Desktop Background Rendering Preparation Checklist: Displays a rendering preparation checklist component on the waiting screen while the pet is generated. (why: The waiting step on home has a high mean duration (2336s) and median (201s), causing drop-off.)
3: [choose_path, new_flow] Companion Path Selection Overview Flow: Introduces an overview screen before path selection to set expectations about quick setup versus custom creation. (why: Choose path screen shows a long mean time (514s), indicating user indecision before selecting a path.)
4: [choose_path, hint] Starter Path Account Persistence Hint: Displays a reassurance hint on path selection explaining that progress on any path is automatically bound to the account. (why: Users hesitate at path selection (mean time 514s) due to uncertainty about saving progress.)
5: [adoption, new_screen] Desktop Companion Customization Confirmation Screen: Adds a confirmation screen after photo upload to confirm successful pet customization before final adoption. (why: Custom pet generation fails or looks wrong for several users, driving adoption drop-off.)
6: [sign_in, copy] Existing Pet Account Sign-In Headline: Updates headline and body copy on sign-in to emphasize restoring existing pet adoptions across devices. (why: Sign-in confusion leads to duplicate account creation and reported missing pets.)
7: [home, wait_info] Desktop Pet Launch Notification Alert Hint: Enables readiness notification and adds a text hint informing users they can minimize the app during generation. (why: Waiting step takes a long time (mean 2336s), causing users to abandon or assume the app stalled.)

scores.note: Pet control tutorial screens consistently perform well despite needing a new screen.
Account safety/persistence hints consistently win and strong support evidence aligns.
Wait screen activity checklists show mixed/neutral results compared to countdown timers.
Introducing sub-flows before selection steps consistently hurts onboarding performance.
Account persistence hints on path selection reliably reduce user hesitation.
Adding extra confirmation screens during adoption introduces drop-off friction.
Copy updates offer modest gains, but gains are typically lower than predictions.
Notification prompts have shown no clear positive effect on drop-off.
